stem: A 15-year-old girl in a Sydney paediatric clinic has changed friendship groups, joined different extracurricular groups, and is trying out different styles while saying she is “working out where I fit”. Her mother worries this must mean something is seriously wrong. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: This can be a normal part of adolescence, where young people experiment with roles and place increasing importance on peer relationships
This usually means adult personality is already fixed and adolescence is effectively over
This mainly reflects physical puberty and body-image change rather than broader adolescent development
This should be assumed to be pathological even when no other concerning features are described
This shows the adolescent has already reached stable personal values and responsibilities

explanation: Normal adolescent development is the correct interpretation. Experimenting with roles, changing peer groups, and trying out different styles can be expected in adolescence as peer relationships become more important.

rationale: This pattern fits normal adolescent identity exploration rather than pathology.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because experimenting with roles and increasing reliance on peers are normal features of adolescence.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because adolescence is a period of ongoing development, not a time when personality is already fixed.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the vignette is about social identity exploration, not mainly physical puberty or body-image change.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because these behaviours are common in normal adolescence and are not automatically pathological without other concerning features.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because stable values and responsibility typically develop progressively, not as an immediate consequence of trying out identities.
